about.title: Lomita Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Lomita is a small city, but its stretch of Pacific Coast Highway and the busy intersections along Western Avenue and Lomita Boulevard see a steady flow of traffic every day, and public records show dozens of injury collisions each year. Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. tend to bring the heaviest crash activity, likely tied to commuters and weekend traffic funneling through town toward Palos Verdes Drive N or the 405. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the road ahead often involves dealing with insurance adjusters, medical bills, and lost wages all at once. We handle car accident claims for injured Lomita residents, evaluating the crash, managing communication with insurers, and working toward fair compensation. There's no upfront cost, and you decide whether to move forward after speaking with us.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. We can help make sure evidence is preserved and deadlines aren't missed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce Your Recovery
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning your compensation can be reduced by your percentage of fault — even a recorded statement to an insurer can be used to argue you were partly at fault. We can advise you before you say anything on the record.

items.title: No Cap, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, and we work on contingency, so there's no fee unless there's a recovery.

items.question: I was in a crash near Western Avenue and Lomita Boulevard — what should I do first?
items.answer: Seek medical attention even if injuries seem minor, since some symptoms show up later. Try to document the scene with photos and get contact information for witnesses if you're able. Avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney, since anything you say could be used to reduce your claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government vehicle or agency was involved — for example, a city or county vehicle — the notice period can be as short as six months, so it's important to act quickly.

items.question: What does it cost to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. We provide a free case review, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no obligation to move forward after your initial conversation.
